ai.description: This snake reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark brown with yellow spots and a distinctively pointed, shovel-like snout. The tail ends in a small, flat, circular scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis macrorhyncha* is best distinguished by its distinctly pointed, beak-like snout, which is more prominent and acutely tapered than the rounded snouts of other *Uropeltis* species.
ai.habitat: The Anaimalai earth snake inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anaimalai earth snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms and other soft-bodied invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis macrorhyncha* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis macrorhyncha* is endemic to the Anaimalai Hills in the Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
